title: Hysterectomy (womb removal)
what: The surgeon removes the womb. The ovaries are sometimes left and sometimes removed. This is decided ahead of time. The surgery is done through keyhole cuts, through the vagina, or through a cut in the belly.
why: For fibroids, heavy bleeding, endometriosis, a dropped womb, and some tumors, when other treatments did not help or are not suitable.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours; the hospital stay is usually 1 to 5 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and hormones. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you or your relatives ever had blood clots in the veins
If you ever had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Talk with your doctor
prepare.text: Ask your doctor how the surgery will be done, and if your ovaries and cervix will be kept.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, swabs, an ultrasound, an ECG, and sometimes a check-up with a general doctor. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time. Sometimes you are asked to clean out your bowel.

prepare.title: Stockings
prepare.text: You are often asked to wear compression stockings. They protect against blood clots. Check with your clinic.

bring: Things for a few days in hospital
steps: On the day of surgery, you change your clothes and a thin tube is put into a vein
In the operating room you get anesthesia and fall asleep
A thin tube called a catheter is put into your bladder
The surgeon removes the womb using the chosen method
The tissue is sent for testing
You wake up in the recovery room, then you are moved to a regular room
feel: Pain low in the belly. You will get pain medicine
After keyhole surgery, shoulder pain from the gas is common. It passes in 1 to 2 days
Bloody discharge from the vagina for several weeks
after: You can usually get up and walk on the first day. This protects against blood clots
Usually no heavy lifting for 4 to 6 weeks
Sex, tampons, swimming pools, and baths: usually after 6 weeks, or when your doctor allows
You will no longer have periods, and pregnancy will not be possible
If your ovaries were removed, menopause may start. Talk about it with your doctor
Tissue test results usually take 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Heavy bleeding: soaking a pad within an hour
A fever above 38 degrees, or discharge with a bad smell
Severe belly pain, or pain that gets worse
Pain and swelling in a leg
Chest pain or shortness of breath: call emergency services

faq.q: Will I have menopause after a hysterectomy?
faq.a: If your ovaries were kept, usually not. They keep making hormones. If they were removed, menopause starts right away.

faq.q: Can I have sex after a hysterectomy?
faq.a: Yes. Usually after 6 weeks, when everything has healed. Your doctor will tell you exactly when.

faq.q: How long is recovery after a hysterectomy?
faq.a: Usually 2 to 6 weeks, depending on the type of surgery. It is faster after keyhole surgery, and longer after a belly cut.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your things, documents, list of medicines, and stockings, if prescribed. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
